description: Zero-dependency, tree-shakeable utils for Brazilian-specific businesses: CPF, CNPJ, boleto, Pix, CEP, holidays and more.
rules: The package has zero runtime dependencies and ships as ESM plus a UMD build; nothing else needs to be installed to use it.
Import from the root: import { isValidCpf } from '@brazilian-utils/brazilian-utils'. Every util is also a kebab-case subpath, e.g. '@brazilian-utils/brazilian-utils/is-valid-cpf'.
Use the subpaths to lazy-load the dataset-backed utils (getMunicipalities, getMunicipalityByCode, getCnae, getCbo, getCfop, isValidNcm, getBanks): each one embeds a large official table.
Never import the same util from both the root and its subpath in one app: a bundler treats them as two unrelated modules and bundles the dataset twice.
Public functions never throw on bad input (null, undefined, wrong type): isValid* return false, format* and parse* return '', single-item getters return null, list getters return [].
The only utils that reject are the async getAddressInfoByCep (GetAddressInfoByCepError: NotFound, Validation, Service) and getCepInfoByAddress (GetCepInfoByAddressError: NotFound, Validation).
isValid* accept the usual mask characters and whitespace, so there is no need to strip formatting first; format* return the masked string and parse* return the unmasked value.
Alphanumeric CNPJ (IN RFB 2.229/2024): pass { version: 2 } to isValidCnpj, formatCnpj and parseCnpj, and call generateCnpj(2) or generateCnpj({ version: 2 }).
CNPJ version 2 accepts both numeric and alphanumeric values and folds lowercase to uppercase; the default version 1 is numeric only, so parseCnpj without { version: 2 } drops the letters.
CNPJ version 2 has no reserved-value list: a repeated-character alphanumeric base that passes the checksum is valid, unlike the repeated numeric values that version 1 rejects.
The 1.x aliases formatCEP, formatCNPJ, formatCPF, generateCNPJ, generateCPF, isValidCEP, isValidCNPJ, isValidCPF, isValidIE and isValidPIS are deprecated; use the camelCase names.
Deprecated since 2.4.0: getCities (use getMunicipalities, which returns { name, code } objects) and the async getMunicipality (use the synchronous, offline getMunicipalityByCode).
Deprecated since 2.4.0: the positional isValidIe(stateCode, ie), replaced by isValidIe({ value, stateCode }), and the 'widenet' provider of getAddressInfoByCep.
Deprecated since 2.4.0: the *Options type aliases of the single-object-argument functions; use the *Params names (GetHolidaysParams, IsHolidayParams, GetMunicipalityParams, ...).
Every util is synchronous and pure except getAddressInfoByCep, getCepInfoByAddress and the deprecated getMunicipality, which are async; the first two query public CEP APIs over HTTPS.
The generate* utils draw random values with Math.random() (generatePixPayload is the exception, built from its parameters), so use them for tests and fixtures, never for security.
Supported runtimes: Node.js ^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0, Bun, Deno and evergreen browsers. Types ship with the package; import option and result types by name from the root.
